overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to give a member written 48-hour notice of the December 2 executive session; the other allegations were not violations or were declined.

allegations.summary: A board member, as subject of a December 2 executive session on complaints against her, was not given 48 hours' written notice of it.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board failed notify Ms. Briand in writing 48 hours in advance of the December 2 executive session, violating the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The December 15 executive session on complaints against the same board member allegedly lacked 48 hours' written notice to her.
allegations.key_passage: we find no violation with respect to the December 15 executive session, because the Board postponed any discussion of the complaint against Ms. Briand once Ms. Briand informed the Board that she was not notified in writing 48 hours in advance of the executive session.

allegations.summary: The board scheduled a December 28 executive session on complaints against a member who had said she was unavailable until January 4.
allegations.key_passage: As the Board did not meet on December 28, we find no violation with respect to this allegation.

allegations.summary: Draft minutes of the December 2 executive session were alleged to be inaccurate.
allegations.key_passage: We do not find that the Board approved inaccurate minutes of its December 2 executive session meeting, as the minutes are still in draft form.

allegations.summary: Complaints about the chair's Select Board agenda request, members' conduct and Town Counsel contact, and the cease-and-desist order's accuracy were raised but not Open Meeting Law issues.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, these allegations would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25. Accordingly, we decline to review them.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
